clue.text: Upper third of school eats free meals, which degrades teacher's "invitation"

indicators.note: degrading something breaks it down, so the words before are broken up and rebuilt
in a down entry the upper part is the start, and a third of a six-letter word is its opening two letters

parts.note: the opening third of a six-letter word

explanation.surface: Older pupils taking free school dinners is a scandal that reflects badly on the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upper' works because this is a down entry, so the top of school is its start. The quotation marks warn that this invitation is not a welcome one.
explanation.definitionFit: Teachers write this summons on poor work or say it to misbehaving pupils, an ironic sort of invitation to a telling-off.

clue.text: Royals, predominantly, come and go, revelling in sexual activity … none here now

definitions.text: Royals, predominantly, come and go, revelling in sexual activity … none here now

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: rubbing against another person for sexual pleasure; it is split after its third letter

indicators.note: revellers cavort wildly, so the letters are thrown about into a new order
read as pre-dominant, the letter standing in front of all the others

parts.note: the two verbs as written, with the link word dropped

explanation.surface: A racy picture of royal comings and goings at a house that now stands empty.
explanation.walkthrough: The scrambled letters split the sexual activity after its third letter. The whole clue also describes the house, which Harry and Meghan left in 2023.
explanation.definitionFit: Frogmore Cottage, on the Windsor estate, was the home of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex until they vacated it in 2023.

clue.text: Isn't it being overlooked by second Carnival man?

parts.note: it in the old sense of sex appeal, abbreviated
the philosopher's Latin term for an entity or existence

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about something being ignored, perhaps at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'overlooked by' puts the second's letter on top of the rest. It for sex appeal and ens for being are crossword favourites.
explanation.definitionFit: Camille Saint-Saëns composed The Carnival of the Animals, so he is the man behind that famous Carnival.

clue.text: Staying in, waste a chance for publicity

indicators.note: one part stays within the other, lodged in the middle of it

explanation.surface: Staying indoors means you have thrown away your moment in the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like part of the phrase 'staying in', but it stands alone as the word for trendy.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo op is an occasion arranged so that a public figure can be photographed and gain publicity.

clue.text: Terminally, Cleopatra so bitten yesterday?

indicators.note: something bitten is held between the jaws, so it ends up inside

parts.note: 'so bitten' means bitten in the way Cleopatra famously was, by the venomous snake

indicators.note: the terminal letter is the final one of the name that follows

explanation.surface: Was the Egyptian queen bitten by her snake only yesterday?
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into ASP: AS-A-P. 'Yesterday' is the joking office demand for something needed immediately.
explanation.definitionFit: When a boss says they want work done yesterday, they mean as soon as possible, so the abbreviation fits.

clue.text: Game 6: Olympian driving German car — he scores

parts.note: Sebastian Coe, the British Olympic runner
someone driving is in the vehicle

explanation.surface: A board game result, then an athlete at the wheel of an Audi who keeps scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: LUDO + VI + COE + IN + AUDI. 'He scores' sounds like sport but means writing music.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludovico Einaudi is an Italian composer and pianist, and a composer writes musical scores.

clue.text: A happy day in prospect at the Abbey?

definitions.text: A happy day in prospect at the Abbey?

parts.note: surface reading: a forthcoming celebration such as a wedding day
setter's reading: the betrothal of the monk who ranks next below an abbot

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally means an existing commitment used as an excuse; here it is read as a prior being engaged to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: A prior is a monastic official, so his engagement to be married would promise a happy wedding day at the abbey.

clue.text: Blame argument for cutting hand

indicators.note: something cutting into a word slices into its middle and sits there

parts.note: to hand or pass something across
a pro is a point in favour

explanation.surface: Fault-finding over a debate about whether to cut a hand of cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is a verb here, as in hand me the salt, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to criticise or find fault with them, a close synonym of blaming them.

clue.text: Old fogey just quits

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a conventional, unfashionable person
second meaning: fair and even, with nothing owed either way

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an old man simply giving up. 'Just' and 'quits' each also mean the answer alone (fair; level).
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a dull conventional person, and as an adjective means fair or settled, with neither party owing anything.

clue.text: One's apparently not informed m'colleague

parts.note: one is, from the speaker's own point of view, contracted

explanation.surface: Someone admitting to being out of the loop, mentioning a fellow worker.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M + O + GEN. Gen is British slang for information; m'colleague is the setter speaking of a fellow Guardian compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is another setter in the Guardian's team of cryptic compilers, so a workmate of Enigmatist.

clue.text: In games, two out of three forwards appear overall

indicators.note: the games letters go in among the repeated words

parts.note: to as in to and fro means forwards; three of them
says the two letters of games are spread out among the three words

explanation.surface: Sporting forwards turning up in most matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Forwards is not football here but the word in to and fro. The games letters do not stay together: one follows the first forward and the other closes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: From head to foot means completely, covering the whole of something, which is what overall means as an adverb.

clue.text: Knock here — radio presenter dressing!
Standard supplement for contract worker at Victoria Station?

parts.note: stock as an adjective: usual, standard
a clause added to a contract

explanation.surface: Contract staff at a London railway terminus getting extra pay.
explanation.walkthrough: Victoria Station is not the London terminus: a station is an Australian ranch, and Victoria is an Australian state.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockrider is an Australian herdsman who rides after cattle on a sheep or cattle station.

clue.text: Club badly broken during Hitler's short war

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls within it
cut short, the German word loses its final letter
something done badly is messed up, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A weapon smashed during the Second World War.
explanation.walkthrough: Hitler's tells you the word for war is German; short drops its last letter before the jumbled word goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A knobkerrie is a short wooden club with a knobbed head, used as a weapon in southern Africa.

clue.text: Salon's No 1 supporter given a vessel for immersion

indicators.note: number one in the word is its leading letter

parts.note: a golf tee supports the ball
a as in so much a head

explanation.surface: The salon's top backer is presented with a dish for soaking things.
explanation.walkthrough: S + TEE + PER. 'A' for per is easy to miss among small words.
explanation.definitionFit: To steep is to soak something in liquid, so a steeper is a container in which things are immersed, as tea or grain.

clue.text: Town branch taking delivery of precious commodity

indicators.note: something that takes delivery receives it and holds it within

parts.note: a large branch of a tree

explanation.surface: A local branch office receiving a shipment of gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Branch' sounds like a bank office, not a tree. Or is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is a town with its own corporation or a district of a city with self-government.

clue.text: Wander here, when prowler's night finally becomes day

indicators.note: one letter turns into another, swapping it out of the word
finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A night-time stalker's habits change when daylight comes.
explanation.walkthrough: TIGRESS has its initial T (the last letter of night) changed to D for day.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to wander away from the main subject in speech or writing.

clue.text: Means to get to Hogwarts chambers in two seconds

indicators.note: the chambers sit in between the pair of seconds

parts.note: B for second-class, and a tick, a moment

explanation.surface: Getting to the Harry Potter school and finding your rooms in no time.
explanation.walkthrough: The two seconds are of different kinds: the letter for second-class and a word for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Witches and wizards in the Harry Potter books fly on these, so one is a means of travel to the school.

clue.text: Uncassocked choirboy maybe depressing clergyman

indicators.note: removing the cassock strips away the outer layer, so the outside letters go

parts.note: a choirboy is an example of one who sings

explanation.surface: A choirboy out of his robe getting a clergyman down.
explanation.walkthrough: SINGER loses its outer S and R. William Inge, Dean of St Paul's, was nicknamed the Gloomy Dean.
explanation.definitionFit: Dean Inge was famous for pessimistic sermons and writings, earning the name the Gloomy Dean, hence a depressing churchman.

clue.text: Veteran car — Model T, I suspect — about to be driven away

indicators.note: suspect here means dodgy, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order
something driven away leaves, so those letters are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone eyeing an early Ford and guessing it is a vintage motor.
explanation.walkthrough: CAR loses CA to leave R, which joins MODELTI for the rearrangement. 'Veteran car' looks like one phrase but car is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-timer is someone with long experience of something, which is what a veteran is.

clue.text: Our race times, from the people staging the Tourist Trophy

definitions.text: from the people staging the Tourist Trophy

explanation.surface: A speaker on how fast our team ran at the famous motorcycle races.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN + X. The Tourist Trophy (TT) is the motorcycle race held on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: Manx is the adjective for things from the Isle of Man, the island whose people host the TT races.

clue.text: Champion FC's no longer ad-free action arenas

indicators.note: what is no longer there has been taken out of the name

parts.note: the Spanish football club, many times European champions, with its possessive
ad plus rid, a word for free

explanation.surface: A winning football club finally free of sponsors' advertising in its stadiums.
explanation.walkthrough: Take ADRID out of REAL MADRID'S to leave REALM-S. 'Ad-free' looks like a description but spells out the letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are spheres or domains of activity, fields in which action takes place.

clue.text: Perhaps 9 is impossible, on reflection

indicators.note: a mirror image runs the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a no-go is something that cannot happen

explanation.surface: A thought that something may be impossible, after further consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 refers to the answer at 9 across; only the second word is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: An isogon is a polygon with all angles equal, and a square, the answer to 9, is an example of one.

clue.text: On the slide not one is playful

indicators.note: not one means without one, so the letter for one is removed

parts.note: taken as written; I stands for one

explanation.surface: Someone joking that nobody is falling behind.
explanation.walkthrough: IS without its I leaves S, then KIDDING.
explanation.definitionFit: Skidding means sliding out of control, so a skidding car is on the slide.
